topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the instructor background, and sets out the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiological concepts, environmental risk, and cancer epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, balancing intrinsic mutation risk against environmental exposures through epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral mechanisms in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and oncogenic viruses drive malignancy, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed mechanistic case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms through which physical radiation and chemical compounds undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how non-mutagenic promoters, developmental windows, and tissue-specific microenvironments facilitate the expansion of initiated cells into malignancies.

topics.label: Methods for identifying, testing, and evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to establish carcinogen causality and assess exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a final wrap-up of the main themes and closing remarks.
